Wymore.title: Wymore Transfer
Wymore.html:
Supporting Evidence

Traffic is real and engaged on some days (scroll hit 97% on 08.16), yet not one visitor has opted in. With capture ruled out, that points to the page's offer/CTA failing to persuade — or the audience being the wrong fit. Ad 01.02 is dead (0 clicks).

Hypotheses

  1. Page 1 offer/CTA is weak or unclear — engaged visitors don't see a reason to opt in. (high)
  2. Traffic/audience mismatch — clicks come from low-intent users who won't convert. (medium)
  3. Scroll is volatile (25%–97%) — some visitors may not reach the form on low-scroll days. (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: rework the Page 1 offer/CTA to drive opt-ins. Since capture works and traffic arrives, the single highest-value lever is the page's value proposition + call-to-action. Use Mouseflow to see exactly where visitors drop before opting in, then revise the headline/offer/CTA around that point. (If a rebuilt offer still gets 0%, the next test is the audience.)

Expected Result & Economics

Moving Page 1 from 0% toward even a 10–15% opt-in turns the traffic already being bought (~91 visitors) into real leads and a first measurable CPL — the account's first leads in a week.

Approval Needed

Page 1 offer/CTA revision — align on scope. No budget change needed to test it.

Changes Made / Learning

Change log: 08.17 — lead capture tested and confirmed working (shows in GHL) — Juan. Learning: This reframes the account. Earlier docs treated 0 leads as a possible tracking break; with capture verified, it's a genuine Page 1 conversion problem. Ad, capture, and (on good days) scroll are fine — the offer/CTA is what isn't converting.

Change log: none documented. Learning: strong page, expensive traffic — volume is the limiter.

GRNDED.title: Grnded Agency
GRNDED.html:
Supporting Evidence

Grnded consistently runs a very high CPM (~$100+) and thin click volume. Today's CTR under 1% made clicks especially pricey. The page isn't the problem (leads still came) — the ad economics are.

Hypotheses

  1. Expensive, narrow audience — high CPM + low CTR = costly clicks. (high)
  2. Page 1 still converts fine. (high)

Recommended Action

One change (continuity): the lever is ad cost, not the page. Hold today (interim); if CTR stays <1% and CPC high on the fresh snapshot, test a broader/cheaper audience.

Expected Result

Lower CPM/CPC → more clicks at the same spend → more leads from an already-converting page.

Approval Needed

None today.

Changes Made / Learning

Change log: none documented. Learning: Grnded's constraint is cost-of-traffic; the page converts well.

Supporting Evidence

Ad 2.01 · 3-day trend

Metric 08.12 08.13 08.14
CTR 2.49% 1.46% 1.92%
GHL Leads 1 4 0
Unbounce Conv (cum) 4 4 5

Engagement is fine and the page CR (~22%) is the strongest of the group. But GHL shows 0 while the page shows a new conversion — either an attribution lag or a capture gap. Volume is low (6 clicks), so a single 0-lead day could also be normal variance.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. Tracking/attribution gap — a lead converted on-page but didn't register in GHL (or is lagging). (high)
  2. Genuine low-volume variance — 6 clicks can produce a 0-lead day by chance. (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: verify today's lead in GHL — reconcile the Unbounce +1 conversion against GHL (check for a lagged or lost lead). Grnded's page is the strongest of the group (~22% CR), so protecting the lead-capture path is the highest-value move before touching budget or creative.

Expected Result

Either the missing lead appears in GHL (attribution lag confirmed, no problem) or we catch a capture gap early — before scaling spend into a leaky tracker.

Approval Needed

None — this is a verification step, no budget change.

Learning Captured

Open. Strong ad + strong page, but a 4 → 0 GHL lead drop with a page conversion unaccounted for. Confirm tracking before reading too much into one low-volume day.

GRNDED.title: Grnded Agency
GRNDED.html:
Supporting Evidence

Ad 2.01 · 2-day trend

Metric 08.12 08.13
Spend $25.10 $43.61
CTR 2.49% 1.46%
CPC $4.18 $7.27
GHL Leads 1 4
Real CPL $25.10 $10.90

More budget produced more leads at a much better CPL — the account is scaling efficiently. The softening CTR and flat click count (6 despite +74% spend) suggest the added spend is buying pricier impressions (CPM ~$106), worth monitoring so CTR doesn't slide under 1%.

Hypotheses (1–3)

  1. Added budget reached more qualified people who converted — scaling is working. (high)
  2. CTR softened as the audience widened, but it's still healthy (1.46%). (medium)
  3. The page is relatively strong (~20% CR, near the 25–30% target). (medium)

Recommended Action

One change: continue scaling Ad 2.01's budget. It's the clear winner — leads 1 → 4, CPL down to $10.90 — so the single best move is to keep feeding it, while watching CTR (keep it above 1%) and CPC as spend grows. Hold the creative and page constant so the scale effect reads clean.

Expected Result

Continued lead growth with CPL holding around $10 or better. If CTR slides toward 1% or CPC keeps climbing as we scale, that flags the efficient-spend ceiling and the ad becomes the next thing to address.

Approval Needed

Budget increase on Ad 2.01 needs your sign-off. (Note: adding Mouseflow scroll tracking for this client would complete the picture — it's the only one without it.)

Learning Captured

Strong second day: leads 1 → 4, CPL $25 → $11, page CR ~20% (best of the group). Scaling is working; watch CTR/CPC as spend rises.
